Después de usar la librería de imputación scikit-learn es posible crear las matrices de varianzas y covarianzas
```{python}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
exp_year = pd.read_csv('BD_2022_test_imputed.csv')
data = exp_year
cols = data.columns[1:data.shape[1]]
display(cols)
data = data[cols]
means = np.mean(data, axis = 0)

data_center = data-means
data_center.head
display(np.transpose(data_center) @ data_center/data_center.shape[0])

import seaborn as sns

r=data.corr()
sns.heatmap(
    r,
    annot=True,  # Write the data values in the cells
    fmt=".2f",  # Format numbers to 2 decimal places
    cmap="coolwarm",  # Color map scheme
    vmin=-1,
    vmax=1,  # Set colorbar limits (useful for correlations)
    linewidths=0.5,  # Add subtle borders between cells
    cbar=True,  # Show colorbar legend
)
plt.show()
```
